findings.problem: fs::read_to_string(path).unwrap() - unwrap on fallible I/O panics when file is missing, unreadable, or path is invalid
findings.failure_mode: untrusted filesystem input aborts the entire process instead of returning a typed I/O or parse error
findings.fix: Return Result<Vec<Record>, io::Error> (or a typed error enum) and propagate with ? instead of unwrap()

findings.problem: parts[0] and parts[1] - unchecked indexing on a split result that may have fewer than 2 elements
findings.failure_mode: malformed CSV line with fewer than 2 fields panics at runtime via index-out-of-bounds
findings.fix: Use parts.get(0) and parts.get(1).ok_or(ParseError::Invalid) with typed error, or use split_once(',')

findings.problem: parts[1].parse::<u32>().unwrap() as u16 - lossy as cast from u32 to u16 silently truncates values > 65535
findings.failure_mode: sensor value 70000 parses to u32 then truncates to 34467, silently corrupting domain data with no error signal
findings.fix: Use u16::try_from(parsed_u32).map_err(|_| ParseError::Overflow) or parse directly as u16 with .parse::<u16>().map_err(...)

findings.problem: println!("loaded {}", parts[0]) - println is hidden I/O fused inside the data-loading logic
findings.failure_mode: side effects in pure-logic path make the function non-deterministic, break functional core, and leak implementation details into domain code
findings.fix: Move all println/logging to the shell layer; load_sensors should be pure data conversion returning only Records

findings.problem: Raw primitives (String from split, u32 from parse) cross the parse boundary into Record without fallible smart constructor validation
findings.failure_mode: callers can construct invalid domain states directly; no validation that name is non-empty or value is in domain range before Record is created
findings.fix: Create Record via a constructor: impl Record { fn from_parts(name: &str, value: &str) -> Result<Self, ParseError> { ... } } with all validation inside

findings.problem: use std::fs; - file I/O is fused directly into the function that also does parsing and domain construction, violating Data/Calculations/Actions separation
findings.failure_mode: cannot test parsing logic in isolation; cannot swap I/O implementations; violates functional core / imperative shell architecture
findings.fix: Split into shell function (read_file -> String) and pure parser function (String -> Vec<Record>); inject file reading as a separate action layer

findings.problem: load_sensors returns Vec<Record> with no error type; all failures are communicated through panic
findings.failure_mode: caller cannot distinguish between file-not-found, malformed CSV, invalid value, or allocation failure; all manifest as runtime panic
findings.fix: Return Result<Vec<Record>, SensorError> where SensorError is an enum with variants like Io(io::Error), InvalidLine(usize), ParseError(usize), Overflow(usize)

findings.problem: No domain cap on number of records; no try_reserve before collecting into Vec; unbounded allocation from untrusted file size
findings.failure_mode: an attacker or misconfigured sensor can supply a file with millions of lines, causing unbounded memory allocation and potential OOM denial of service
findings.fix: Validate max_items before parsing; use Vec::new() then out.try_reserve(min(line_count, max_items)).map_err(|_| Error::Allocation)?; enforce max_items cap before each push

findings.problem: line.split(',').map(...).collect() allocates a full Vec for every line when only two fields exist
findings.failure_mode: unnecessary allocation per line increases memory pressure and GC burden; split_once would avoid all intermediate Vec allocation for fixed two-field records

findings.problem: Record uses pub name: String - raw primitive String for a domain identifier that likely has format rules (non-empty, specific charset, etc.)
findings.failure_mode: empty string, whitespace-only, or malformed names silently stored as valid sensor identifiers; no domain invariants enforced at the type level
findings.fix: Create a SensorName newtype: pub struct SensorName(String); impl SensorName { fn from_str(s: &str) -> Result<Self, ParseError>; }
